stem: Which child and foreign body scenario is appropriate for the interim honey regimen while awaiting theatre?

options.text: Child older than 1 year, oesophageal button battery, within 12 hours of ingestion, while awaiting theatre
Child younger than 1 year, any swallowed object, while awaiting imaging
Child older than 1 year, non-battery object already beyond the oesophagus
Child of any age with a fish bone causing local discomfort while awaiting CT
Child older than 1 year with suspected airway aspiration and unilateral hyperinflation

explanation: Interim honey use is appropriate for a child older than 1 year with an oesophageal button battery ingested within the previous 12 hours while awaiting theatre.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf p.142

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the interim honey regimen is reserved for children older than 1 year with an oesophageal button battery within 12 hours of ingestion while awaiting theatre.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the regimen is not used in infants and is not recommended for any swallowed object.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the honey regimen applies to a button battery lodged in the oesophagus, not to an object already beyond the oesophagus.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because fish bone ingestion is not the indication for this honey regimen.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because suspected airway aspiration is a different problem from oesophageal button battery ingestion.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
